rites.name: Kalusanum
rites.text: Kalusanum is the concept of the first hush in Ryelora, the moment during the Seeding when the makers sink the Weave into the ground and the sleeping powers settle like silt. It is less a thing than a pause in which every dormant force waits to be named.

rites.name: Sheithis
rites.text: Sheithis is the concept of a living bond between root and rune, held in the Arcane Realm of Ryelora during its earliest Age. It was the thread the first sovereign pulled to swear the Pact that mended the broken worlds of the Sundering. It lives on in every grove that still remembers the oath.

rites.name: Crunar
rites.text: Crunar is a concept of Ryelora, a dreaming current that surfaced during the Sundering, when the old worlds split into Shards and the Pact of the groves was sworn. It is said to be the quiet intention behind the first sovereign's growing kingdoms, a thread of purpose more than a body.

rites.name: Thouggak
rites.text: Thouggak is a concept of Ryelora's Walled Age, an idea of walls that hold back a silent tide and the orders that keep the watch over centuries of stone. It stands as the principle behind the first crossings, where the wall is opened only by those sworn to close it again.

rites.name: Moreldodar
rites.text: Moreldodar is a concept in the Arcane Realm of Ryelora, personified as the principle that a held wall is a promise kept across generations. It is remembered in the Walled Age through the orders, churches and first crossings that grew up around its doctrine of endurance.

rites.name: Kalusarala
rites.text: Kalusarala is a concept of the Arcane Realm in Ryelora, personified as the principle that a single choice splits the world into three futures, each kept on its own shelf of the Library. Its acts are measured by the flames and temple-orders of the Holy Age, where a branch of fate can be lit or sealed.

rites.name: Goukozhun
rites.text: Goukozhun is the concept of the branching hour in Ryelora's Arcane Realm, the moment when the Three Futures diverge and the Library quietly shelves each outcome. Its devotees in the Holy Age of flame and temples treat it as both a warning and a promise, kindling lamps that burn for every possible ending at once.
